Draft:

Phones and the Driver's Seat

Almost everyone I know carries a phone, and almost everyone I know has looked at it while driving. That includes me. I once glanced down at a text at a red light, and when I looked up the light had been green long enough for the driver behind me to honk. Nothing happened, but it showed me how quickly my attention had left the road. For that reason I believe drivers should not be allowed to hold or handle a phone while a vehicle is moving, though I would stop short of banning every possible use.

The case against handheld use is simple. Driving requires eyes, hands, and attention, and a phone takes all three. Reading a message takes about five seconds, and at highway speed a car covers the length of a football field in that time. A driver who is typing is not steering well, not watching mirrors, and not ready to brake. The person who pays for that mistake is often someone else: a child crossing the street, a cyclist, or a family in the next lane. A message can wait ten minutes. An injury cannot be undone.

Some people argue that they are skilled enough to do both. I doubt it. Nobody feels distracted while they are distracted, which is exactly why the habit is dangerous. Confidence is not the same as ability, and the law should not depend on each driver's opinion of himself.

Still, I do not think a total ban makes sense. Phones now serve as maps, and a mounted phone giving spoken directions is safer than a paper map on the passenger seat or a lost driver making sudden turns. A driver should also be able to call for help in an emergency. Hands-free calls are harder to judge, since a conversation still pulls the mind away from traffic, but a short voice call is closer to talking with a passenger than to texting.

So the rule I would support is this: set the route before leaving, mount the phone, and do not touch it again until the car is parked. Navigation and emergency calls stay legal; texting, scrolling, and holding the phone do not. That rule asks very little of drivers and protects everyone who shares the road with them.
